verses.pali: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
verses.english: So I have heard.

verses.pali: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṁ viharati pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde.
verses.english: Now at that time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Sāvatthī in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery.

verses.pali: Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi:
verses.english: There Sāriputta addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: “āvuso bhikkhave”ti.
verses.english: “Reverends, mendicants!”

verses.pali: “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Reverend,” they replied.

verses.pali: Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca:
verses.english: Sāriputta said this:

verses.pali: “ajjhattasaṁyojanañca, āvuso, puggalaṁ desessāmi bahiddhāsaṁyojanañca.
verses.english: “I will teach you about an individual fettered internally and one fettered externally.

verses.pali: Taṁ suṇātha, sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
verses.english: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

verses.pali: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṁ.
verses.english: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.

verses.pali: Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca:
verses.english: Sāriputta said this:

verses.pali: “Katamo cāvuso, ajjhattasaṁyojano puggalo?
verses.english: “Who is an individual fettered internally?

verses.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
verses.english: It’s a mendicant who is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

verses.pali: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in one of the orders of gods.

verses.pali: So tato cuto āgāmī hoti, āgantā itthattaṁ.
verses.english: When they pass away from there, they’re a returner, who comes back to this place.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccati, āvuso, ajjhattasaṁyojano puggalo āgāmī hoti, āgantā itthattaṁ.
verses.english: This is called an individual who is fettered internally, a returner, who comes back to this place.

verses.pali: Katamo cāvuso, bahiddhāsaṁyojano puggalo?
verses.english: Who is an individual fettered externally?

verses.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṁvarasaṁvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno, aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
verses.english: It’s a mendicant who is ethical, restrained in the monastic code, conducting themselves well and resorting for alms in suitable places. Seeing danger in the slightest fault, they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

verses.pali: So aññataraṁ santaṁ cetovimuttiṁ upasampajja viharati.
verses.english: They enter and remain in a certain peaceful state of freed mind.

verses.pali: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they’re reborn in one of the orders of gods.

verses.pali: So tato cuto anāgāmī hoti, anāgantā itthattaṁ.
verses.english: When they pass away from there, they’re a non-returner, not coming back to this place.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso, bahiddhāsaṁyojano puggalo anāgāmī hoti, anāgantā itthattaṁ.
verses.english: This is called an individual who is fettered externally, a non-returner, who does not come back to this place.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, āvuso, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti …pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu.
verses.english: Furthermore, a mendicant is ethical … they keep the rules they’ve undertaken.

verses.pali: So kāmānaṁyeva nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: They simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding sensual pleasures.

verses.pali: So bhavānaṁyeva nibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: They simply practice for disillusionment, dispassion, and cessation regarding future lives.

verses.pali: So taṇhākkhayāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: They practice for the ending of craving.

verses.pali: So lobhakkhayāya paṭipanno hoti.
verses.english: They practice for the ending of greed.

verses.pali: So kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā aññataraṁ devanikāyaṁ upapajjati.
verses.english: When their body breaks up, after death, they are reborn in one of the orders of gods.

verses.pali: So tato cuto anāgāmī hoti, anāgantā itthattaṁ.
verses.english: When they pass away from there, they are non-returners, not coming back to this place.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ vuccatāvuso, bahiddhāsaṁyojano puggalo anāgāmī hoti, anāgantā itthattan”ti.
verses.english: This is called an individual who is fettered externally, a non-returner, who does not come back to this place.”

verses.pali: Atha kho sambahulā samacittā devatā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho tā devatā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: Then several peaceful-minded deities went up to the Buddha, bowed, stood to one side, and said to the Buddha,

verses.pali: “eso, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde bhikkhūnaṁ ajjhattasaṁyojanañca puggalaṁ deseti bahiddhāsaṁyojanañca.
verses.english: “Sir, Venerable Sāriputta is in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery, where he is teaching the mendicants about an individual with internal fetters and one with external fetters.

verses.pali: Haṭṭhā, bhante, parisā.
verses.english: The assembly is overjoyed!

verses.pali: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
verses.english: Sir, please go to Venerable Sāriputta out of sympathy.”

verses.pali: Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.
verses.english: The Buddha consented with silence.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā—seyyathāpi nāma balavā puriso samiñjitaṁ vā bāhaṁ pasāreyya, pasāritaṁ vā bāhaṁ samiñjeyya; evamevaṁ—jetavane antarahito pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde āyasmato sāriputtassa sammukhe pāturahosi.
verses.english: Then the Buddha, as easily as a strong person would extend or contract their arm, vanished from Jeta’s Grove and reappeared in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery, in front of Sāriputta.

verses.pali: Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane.
verses.english: He sat on the seat spread out.

verses.pali: Āyasmāpi kho sāriputto bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi.
verses.english: Sāriputta bowed to the Buddha and sat down to one side.

verses.pali: Ekamantaṁ nisinnaṁ kho āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said to him:

verses.pali: “Idha, sāriputta, sambahulā samacittā devatā yenāhaṁ tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā maṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho, sāriputta, tā devatā maṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: “Just now, Sāriputta, several peaceful-minded deities came up to me, bowed, and stood to one side. Those deities said to me:

verses.pali: ‘eso, bhante, āyasmā sāriputto pubbārāme migāramātupāsāde bhikkhūnaṁ ajjhattasaṁyojanañca puggalaṁ deseti bahiddhāsaṁyojanañca.
verses.english: ‘Sir, Venerable Sāriputta is in the stilt longhouse of Migāra’s mother in the Eastern Monastery, where he is teaching the mendicants about an individual with internal fetters and one with external fetters.

verses.pali: Haṭṭhā, bhante, parisā.
verses.english: The assembly is overjoyed!

verses.pali: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yena āyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā’ti.
verses.english: Sir, please go to Venerable Sāriputta out of sympathy.’

verses.pali: Tā kho pana, sāriputta, devatā dasapi hutvā vīsampi hutvā tiṁsampi hutvā cattālīsampi hutvā paññāsampi hutvā saṭṭhipi hutvā āraggakoṭinitudanamattepi tiṭṭhanti, na ca aññamaññaṁ byābādhenti.
verses.english: Those deities, though they number ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, or sixty, can stand on the point of a needle without bumping up against each other.

verses.pali: Siyā kho pana, sāriputta, evamassa:
verses.english: Sāriputta, you might think:

verses.pali: ‘tattha nūna tāsaṁ devatānaṁ tathā cittaṁ bhāvitaṁ yena tā devatā dasapi hutvā vīsampi hutvā tiṁsampi hutvā cattālīsampi hutvā paññāsampi hutvā saṭṭhipi hutvā āraggakoṭinitudanamattepi tiṭṭhanti na ca aññamaññaṁ byābādhentī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Surely those deities, since so many of them can stand on the point of a needle without bumping up against each other, must have developed their minds in that place.’

verses.pali: Na kho panetaṁ, sāriputta, evaṁ daṭṭhabbaṁ.
verses.english: But you should not see it like this.

verses.pali: Idheva kho, sāriputta, tāsaṁ devatānaṁ tathā cittaṁ bhāvitaṁ, yena tā devatā dasapi hutvā …pe… na ca aññamaññaṁ byābādhenti.
verses.english: It was right here that those deities developed their minds.

verses.pali: Tasmātiha, sāriputta, evaṁ sikkhitabbaṁ:
verses.english: So you should train like this:

verses.pali: ‘santindriyā bhavissāma santamānasā’ti.
verses.english: ‘We shall have peaceful faculties and peaceful minds.’

verses.pali: Evañhi vo, sāriputta, sikkhitabbaṁ.
verses.english: That’s how you should train.

verses.pali: ‘Santindriyānañhi vo, sāriputta, santamānasānaṁ santaṁyeva kāyakammaṁ bhavissati santaṁ vacīkammaṁ santaṁ manokammaṁ.
verses.english: When your faculties and mind are peaceful, your acts of body, speech, and mind will be peaceful, thinking:

verses.pali: Santaṁyeva upahāraṁ upaharissāma sabrahmacārīsū’ti.
verses.english: ‘We shall present the gift of peace to our spiritual companions.’

verses.pali: ‘Evañhi vo, sāriputta, sikkhitabbaṁ.
verses.english: That’s how you should train.

verses.pali: Anassuṁ kho, sāriputta, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā ye imaṁ dhammapariyāyaṁ nāssosun’”ti.
verses.english: Those wanderers of other religions, Sāriputta, who have not heard this exposition of the teaching are lost.”
